58.title: Weak Lefschetz property for codimension-three Artinian Gorenstein algebras
58.statement:
Let $\Bbbk$ be a field of characteristic zero and let
$$
A=\Bbbk[x,y,z]/I
$$
be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra of embedding dimension three. The algebra $A$ has the **weak Lefschetz property** if there is a linear form $\ell\in A_1$ such that every multiplication map
$$
\times\ell:A_i\longrightarrow A_{i+1}
$$
has maximal rank.

**Conjecture.** Every standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra of embedding dimension three over a field of characteristic zero has the weak Lefschetz property.

By Macaulay duality, such an algebra can be written as
$$
A\cong\Bbbk[x,y,z]/\operatorname{Ann}(F),
$$
where $F\in\Bbbk[X,Y,Z]$ is a homogeneous ternary form and $x,y,z$ act by differentiation. Thus a prospective counterexample is specified by finitely many coefficients. If
$$
\ell=ax+by+cz,
$$
then the matrices of the maps $\times\ell$ have entries polynomial—in fact linear—in $a,b,c$. The weak Lefschetz property asks whether some $[a:b:c]\in\mathbb P^2$ makes all these matrices have maximal rank. Failure can therefore be expressed exactly through their maximal minors and rank-drop loci.

**Known reductions and cases.** It is enough to study compressed Gorenstein algebras of odd socle degree. The first formerly open Hilbert function
$$
(1,3,6,6,3,1)
$$
has been settled affirmatively. More recent work proves the weak Lefschetz property when the Sperner number is at most the socle degree plus one; in codimension three, the remaining unknown regime has both socle degree and Sperner number greater than six.

A concrete computational target is to sample or construct ternary dual generators $F$, form the catalecticant and multiplication matrices symbolically, and eliminate $a,b,c$ from the maximal-minor conditions. This could either produce a genuine counterexample or reveal structural identities forcing a Lefschetz element.

315895.title: Kazhdan–Lusztig conjectures
315895.statement:
Let $W$ be a Coxeter group with generating set $S$, let
$\ell(w)$ denote the length of $w \in W$ (the smallest number of elements of $S$
in a product expressing $w$), and let $\leq$ denote the Bruhat order on $W$.

Let $H$ be the Hecke algebra of $W$: the free module over
$\mathbb{Z}[q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}]$ with basis $\{T_w\}_{w \in W}$ and multiplication
determined by

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{y}T_{w}&=T_{yw},&&\text{if }\ell (yw)=\ell (y)+\ell (w),\\(T_{s}+1)(T_{s}-q)&=0,&&\text{if }s\in S.\end{aligned}
$$

Each $T_s$ is invertible, with $T_s^{-1}=q^{-1}T_s+q^{-1}-1$, and
$H$ carries a ring involution $D$ with
$D(q^{1/2})=q^{-1/2}$ and $D(T_w)=T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$ for all $w \in W$.

The Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials are the unique family $\{P_{y,w}\}_{y,w \in W}$
of polynomials in $q$ with integer coefficients such that $P_{y,w}=0$ unless
$y \leq w$, $P_{w,w}=1$, $\deg P_{y,w} \leq
\tfrac{1}{2}(\ell(w)-\ell(y)-1)$ whenever $y<w$, and the elements

$$
C'_{w}=q^{-\frac{\ell (w)}{2}}\sum _{y\leq w}P_{y,w}\,T_{y}
$$

satisfy $D(C'_w)=C'_w$ for all $w \in W$.

Now let
$\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra whose Weyl group is the finite Weyl group $W$,
let $\rho$ be the half-sum of the positive roots, and let $w_0$ be the element
of maximal length in $W$. For $w \in W$ let $M_w$ be the Verma module over
$\mathfrak{g}$ of highest weight $-w(\rho)-\rho$, and let
$L_w$ be its irreducible quotient, the simple highest weight module of highest weight $-w(\rho)-\rho$.
Write
$\operatorname{ch}(X)$ for the formal character of a locally finite weight module $X$.

Then for every $w \in W$,

$$
\operatorname {ch} (L_{w})=\sum _{y\leq w}(-1)^{\ell (w)-\ell (y)}P_{y,w}(1)\operatorname {ch} (M_{y})
$$

and

$$
\operatorname {ch} (M_{w})=\sum _{y\leq w}P_{w_{0}w,\,w_{0}y}(1)\operatorname {ch} (L_{y}).
$$

315907.title: Dittert conjecture
315907.statement:
For an $n \times n$ matrix $A = [a_{ij}]$ with real entries, let

$$
\operatorname{per}(A) = \sum_{\sigma \in S_n} \prod_{i=1}^{n} a_{i,\sigma(i)},
$$

where the sum is over all permutations $\sigma$ in the symmetric group $S_n$,
and define

$$
\phi(A) = \prod_{i=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij}\right) + \prod_{j=1}^{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} a_{ij}\right) - \operatorname{per}(A).
$$

Let $J_n$ denote the $n \times n$ matrix all of whose entries equal $1$.

For every integer $n \ge 1$ and every $n \times n$ matrix $A = [a_{ij}]$ with
$a_{ij} \ge 0$ for all $i, j$ and

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} a_{ij} = n,
$$

one has

$$
\phi(A) \le \phi\!\left(\tfrac{1}{n} J_n\right) = 2 - \frac{n!}{n^{n}},
$$

with equality if and only if $A = \tfrac{1}{n} J_n$.

315995.title: 1-factorization conjecture
315995.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A $1$-factor of $G$ is a spanning $1$-regular
subgraph of $G$, i.e. a perfect matching. A $1$-factorization of
$G$ is a partition of the edge set $E(G)$ into $1$-factors, and $G$ is called
$1$-factorable if it admits a $1$-factorization.

For every integer $n \ge 1$ and every $k$-regular graph $G$ on $2n$ vertices, if

$$
k \ge n \quad \text{when } n \text{ is odd,} \qquad k \ge n-1 \quad \text{when } n \text{ is even,}
$$

then $G$ is $1$-factorable; that is, $E(G)$ can be partitioned into $k$ pairwise
disjoint perfect matchings of $G$.

315999.title: graceful tree conjecture
315999.statement:
Let $T=(V,E)$ be a finite tree with $m=|E|$ edges. Call a map

$$
f:V\longrightarrow\{0,1,\dots,m\}
$$

a graceful labeling of $T$ if $f$ is injective and the induced edge labels
realize every value in $\{1,2,\dots,m\}$, i.e.

$$
\bigl\{\,|f(u)-f(v)| \;:\; uv\in E\,\bigr\}=\{1,2,\dots,m\}.
$$

(Since $|E|=m$ and the set on the left has $m$ elements, this condition says
exactly that the
$m$ edge differences are pairwise distinct and all lie in $\{1,\dots,m\}$.) A
graph admitting such a labeling is called graceful.

Every finite tree admits a graceful labeling.

316020.title: Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture
316020.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple graph, and for $v\in V$ let $\deg_G(v)$ denote
the number of neighbours of $v$, with $\delta(G)=\min_{v\in
V}\deg_G(v)$. For an integer $\ell\ge 3$, a cycle of length $\ell$ in
$G$ is a sequence of pairwise distinct vertices $v_1,v_2,\dots,v_\ell\in
V$ such that $v_iv_{i+1}\in E$ for $1\le i\le \ell-1$ and $v_\ell v_1\in E$.

For every such $G$ with

$$
\delta(G)\ge 3,
$$

there exists an integer $k\ge 2$ such that
$G$ contains a cycle of length $2^{k}$.

316022.title: Grünbaum–Nash-Williams conjecture
316022.statement:
A graph
$G$ is *toroidal* if it admits an embedding in the torus, i.e. there is a drawing of $G$
on the closed orientable surface of genus
$1$ in which vertices are distinct points, edges are arcs joining their endpoints, and no two edges meet except at a common endpoint. A graph $G$
on at least $5$ vertices is *$4$-vertex-connected*
($4$-connected) if it is connected and $G - S$ is connected for every set $S
\subseteq V(G)$ with $|S| \le 3$. A *Hamiltonian cycle* of $G$ is a cycle in
$G$ that passes through every vertex of $G$.

For every finite simple graph $G$: if $G$ is toroidal and
$4$-vertex-connected, then $G$ has a Hamiltonian cycle.

316026.title: Sumner's conjecture
316026.statement:
Call a digraph $T$ a polytree if $T$ is obtained from a (finite, undirected)
tree by assigning to each edge one of its two possible directions, and call a
digraph $D$ a tournament if for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v$ of
$D$ exactly one of the arcs $(u,v)$, $(v,u)$ belongs to $D$. Say that
$D$ contains $T$, written $T \subseteq D$, if there is an injection
$\phi : V(T) \to V(D)$ such that $(\phi(u),\phi(v))$ is an arc of $D$ for every
arc $(u,v)$ of $T$.

For every integer $n \geq 1$, every polytree $T$ on $n$ vertices, and every
tournament $D$ on $2n-2$ vertices,

$$
T \subseteq D.
$$

316037.title: Woodall's conjecture
316037.statement:
Let $D=(V,E)$ be a finite directed graph. For a set $S\subseteq
V$ with $S\neq\emptyset$ and $S\neq V$, write

$$
\partial^+(S)=\{\,uv\in E: u\in S,\ v\in V\setminus S\,\},\qquad \partial^-(S)=\{\,uv\in E: u\in V\setminus S,\ v\in S\,\}.
$$

Call $\partial^+(S)$ a $\emph{dicut}$ of $D$ if $\partial^-(S)=\emptyset$, i.e.
every edge crossing the partition $\{S,V\setminus S\}$ leaves
$S$. A set $J\subseteq E$ is a $\emph{dijoin}$ of $D$ if $J\cap
C\neq\emptyset$ for every dicut $C$ of
$D$; equivalently, contracting the edges of $J$ yields a strongly connected
directed graph.

Suppose $D$ has at least one dicut, and let

$$
k=\min\{\,|C| : C \text{ is a dicut of } D\,\}.
$$

Then there exist pairwise disjoint sets $J_1,\dots,J_k\subseteq E$ such that
each $J_i$ is a dijoin of $D$.

316059.title: Erdős–Turán conjecture on additive bases
316059.statement:
Let $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and for $n \in \mathbb{N}$ define the
representation function

$$
r_B(n) = \#\{(a_1,a_2) \in B^2 \mid a_1 + a_2 = n\},
$$

where the pairs are ordered and $a_1 = a_2$ is allowed. Suppose that
$B$ is an additive basis of order $2$, i.e. there exists $n_0$ such that $r_B(n)
> 0$ for all $n > n_0$. Then

$$
\limsup_{n \to \infty} r_B(n) = \infty.
$$

Equivalently: there is no set $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and constant $C < \infty$
such that $0 < r_B(n) \le C$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

316062.title: Lander, Parkin, and Selfridge conjecture
316062.statement:
Let $k \geq 2$ be an integer and let $m, n \geq 1$ be integers with $m \leq n$.
Suppose that $x_1, \ldots, x_m$ and $y_1, \ldots, y_n$ are positive integers
satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i^{k} = \sum_{j=1}^{n} y_j^{k},
$$

and suppose the equality is nontrivial in the sense that

$$
x_i \neq y_j \quad \text{for all } 1 \leq i \leq m, \ 1 \leq j \leq n,
$$

so that no term occurs on both sides (repetitions of a value within one and the
same side are permitted). Then

$$
m + n \geq k.
$$

Equivalently, for all integers $k \geq 2$ and $m, n \geq 1$ with $m + n < k$,
there exist no positive integers $x_1, \ldots, x_m, y_1, \ldots, y_n$ with
$\sum_{i=1}^{m} x_i^{k} = \sum_{j=1}^{n} y_j^{k}$ and $x_i \neq y_j$ for all
$i, j$.

316164.title: Stanley–Wilf conjecture
316164.statement:
For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ and a permutation
$\beta$ of $\{1,2,\dots,k\}$, say that $\sigma$ contains $\beta$ as a pattern if
there are indices $1\le i_1<i_2<\dots<i_k\le n$ such that, for all
$1\le a<b\le k$,

$$
\sigma(i_a)<\sigma(i_b)\iff \beta(a)<\beta(b),
$$

and say that $\sigma$ avoids $\beta$ otherwise. For $n\ge 1$ let

$$
S_n(\beta)=\{\sigma\in S_n:\ \sigma \text{ avoids } \beta\},
$$

where $S_n$ is the set of all permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$.

For every $k\ge 1$ and every permutation $\beta\in S_k$ there exists a constant
$C=C(\beta)<\infty$ such that

$$
|S_n(\beta)|\le C^{\,n}\qquad\text{for all } n\ge 1;
$$

equivalently, the limit

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|S_n(\beta)|}
$$

exists and is finite.

318034.title: Mean field frozen percolation scaling conjecture
318034.statement:
Let $(\mathcal{V}^N(t))_{t\geq 0}$ be a critical sequence of frozen percolation processes with $\mu(N)=N^{-\alpha}$, where $0<\alpha<1$, and let $m_1^N(t)$ and $m_2^N(t)$ denote the first two component-size moments, while $|\mathcal{C}_{\max}^N(t)|$ is the size of the largest component. For $t_1<t_2$, let $p_k^N[t_1,t_2]$ be the probability that a component burnt during $[t_1,t_2]$ has size $k$. Define

$$
\beta(\alpha):=\begin{cases}2\alpha&\text{if }\alpha\leq\frac13,\\[2pt]\frac{\alpha+1}{2}&\text{if }\alpha\geq\frac13.
\end{cases}
$$

**Mean field frozen percolation scaling conjecture.** For every $T^g<t$,

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\left(\mathbf{E}(m_1^N(t))\right)}{\log N}=\alpha,
$$

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\left(\mathbf{E}(m_2^N(t))\right)-\log\left(\mathbf{E}(m_1^N(t))\right)}{\log N}=\beta(\alpha),
$$

and

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{\log\left(\mathbf{E}(|\mathcal{C}_{\max}^N(t)|)\right)}{\log N}=\beta(\alpha).
$$

Moreover, for every $\underline{\mathbf{v}}(0)$, $T^g<t_1<t_2$, and $\alpha$, there exists a non-defective probability distribution function $F:(0,\infty)\to(0,1)$ with $\lim_{x\to0_+}F(x)=0$ and $\lim_{x\to\infty}F(x)=1$ such that, for all $x\in\mathbb{R}_+$,

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}\sum_{k\geq1}\mathbb{I}[k\leq xN^{\beta(\alpha)}]p_k^N[t_1,t_2]=F(x).
$$

The claim predicts the scaling exponents of component moments and the largest component, together with a limiting law for the size of burnt components. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so it is recorded as open.

326053.title: The partial Frobenius conjecture for cohomology of quaternionic Shimura varieties
326053.statement:
For each $\mathfrak{p}\in\Sigma_p$, let $n_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the smallest positive integer such that $\sigma_{\mathfrak{p}}^{n_{\mathfrak{p}}}\mathtt{S}_\infty=\mathtt{S}_\infty$, and let $d_{\mathfrak{p}}$ be the inertia degree of $\mathfrak{p}$ in $F/\mathbb{Q}$. Assume that whenever $\mathfrak{p}$ splits in $E$ as $\mathfrak{q}\bar{\mathfrak{q}}$, one has $\#\tilde{\mathtt{S}}_{\infty/\mathfrak{q}}=\#\tilde{\mathtt{S}}_{\infty/\bar{\mathfrak{q}}}$. For every Hecke character $\chi\in\mathscr{A}_{E,\tilde\Sigma}^w$, the following equality holds in the Grothendieck group of finitely generated modules over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_l[\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{A}^{\infty,p})][(\Phi_{\mathfrak{p}^2})^{n_{\mathfrak{p}}};\mathfrak{p}\in\Sigma_p]$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\big[ H^\star_{c,\operatorname{et}}(\mathbf{Sh}_{K”_{\mathtt{S},p}}(G”_{\tilde{\mathtt{S}}})_{\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p},\mathscr{L}”^{(\underline{k},w)}_{\tilde{\mathtt{S}},\tilde\Sigma,l})^{\mathbb{A}_E^{\infty,\times}=\chi}\big]
&=(-1)^{g-\#\mathtt{S}_\infty}\big[\bigoplus_{\pi\in\mathscr{A}_{(\underline{k},w)}[\chi_F]}(\pi_{\mathtt{S}}^\infty)^{K_{\mathtt{S},p}}\otimes\tilde\rho_{\pi,l}^{\mathtt{S}}\big]\\
&\quad+\delta_{\underline{k},2}\sum_{\pi\in\mathscr{B}_w[\chi_F]}\big[(\pi_{\mathtt{S}}^\infty)^{K_{\mathtt{S},p}}\otimes\tilde\rho_{\pi,l}^{\mathtt{S}}\big]\otimes\left(\big[(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_l\oplus\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_l(-1))^{\otimes(\Sigma_\infty-\mathtt{S}_\infty)}\big]-\delta_{\mathtt{S},\emptyset}[\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_l]\right).
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\tilde\rho_{\pi,l}^{\mathtt{S}}$ has the same underlying vector space as

$$
\rho_{\pi,l}^{\mathtt{S}}=\bigotimes_{\mathfrak{p}\in\Sigma_p}\left(\bigotimes_{\Sigma_{\infty/\mathfrak{p}}-\mathtt{S}_{\infty/\mathfrak{p}}}\operatorname{-Ind}_{\operatorname{Gal}_{F_{\mathfrak{p}}}}^{\operatorname{Gal}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}}\rho_{\pi,l}|_{\operatorname{Gal}_{F_{\mathfrak{p}}}}\right),
$$

with the specified partial Frobenius actions: $(\Phi_{\mathfrak{p}^2})^{n_{\mathfrak{p}}}$ acts on the $\mathfrak{p}$-factor as $\operatorname{Frob}_{p^{2n_{\mathfrak{p}}}}$ multiplied by $\omega_\pi(\varpi_{\mathfrak{p}})^{n_{\mathfrak{p}}(1-\#\mathtt{S}_{\infty/\mathfrak{p}}/d_{\mathfrak{p}})}$, trivially on the other factors, and by multiplication by $p^2$ on the corresponding Tate twists.

331759.title: The extremal classification conjecture for multiply union families
331759.statement:
For vectors ${\bf x}\in{\mathbb R}^n$, write ${\bf x}=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and define the weight of ${\bf a}\in{\mathbb N}^n$ by

$$
|{\bf a}|=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i.
$$

For vectors in ${\mathbb N}^n$, define their join coordinatewise by

$$
({\bf a}_1\mathop{\vee}\cdots\mathop{\vee}{\bf a}_r)_i=\max\{(\mathbf a_1)_i,\ldots,(\mathbf a_r)_i\}.
$$

A family $A\subseteq{\mathbb N}^n$ is **$r$-wise $s$-union** if $|{\bf a}_1\mathop{\vee}\cdots\mathop{\vee}{\bf a}_r|\leq s$ for all ${\bf a}_1,\ldots,{\bf a}_r\in A$. Let ${\mathcal D}({\bf a})=\{{\bf c}\in{\mathbb N}^n:{\bf c}\prec{\bf a}\}$, where ${\bf c}\prec{\bf a}$ means $c_i\leq a_i$ for every $i$, and let ${\mathcal D}(A)=\bigcup_{{\bf a}\in A}{\mathcal D}({\bf a})$. Define

$$
{\mathcal S}({\bf a},d)=\{{\bf a}+{\boldsymbol\epsilon}\in{\mathbb N}^n:{\boldsymbol\epsilon}\in{\mathbb N}^n,\ |{\boldsymbol\epsilon}|=d\}.
$$

A vector is a **balanced partition** if its coordinates differ pairwise by at most $1$. Writing ${\bf 1}=(1,\ldots,1)$ and $u=n-r+1$, for $0\leq d\leq\lfloor s/r\rfloor$ and $|{\bf a}|=s-rd$, define

$$
K(r,n,{\bf a},d)=\bigcup_{i=0}^{\lfloor d/u\rfloor}{\mathcal D}({\mathcal S}({\bf a}+i{\bf 1},d-ui)).
$$

**The extremal classification conjecture.** Let $r\geq2$ and let $s$ be a positive integer. If $A\subseteq{\mathbb N}^n$ is $r$-wise $s$-union, then

$$
|A|\leq\max_{0\leq d\leq\lfloor s/r\rfloor}|K(r,n,{\bf a},d)|,
$$

where ${\bf a}\in{\mathbb N}^n$ is a balanced partition with $|{\bf a}|=s-rd$. Moreover, if equality holds, then $A=K(r,n,{\bf a},d)$ for some $0\leq d\leq\lfloor s/r\rfloor$.

The problem asks for the maximum size of an $r$-wise $s$-union family and for the extremal families attaining it. The displayed claim identifies the candidate families $K(r,n,{\bf a},d)$, but the supplied text gives no resolution status or evidence that the asserted bound and equality classification are proved.

340094.title: Jelínek's equidistribution bijection conjecture for restricted permutations and Fishburn matrices

344690.title: Successive-maxima conjecture for non-genus class numbers of abelian fields
344690.statement:
Let $G$ be an abelian group and let ${\mathcal K}_G^s$ be the family of abelian fields with Galois group $G$ and signature $s$. For a conductor $f$, let ${\mathcal F}_{G,f}^s$ consist of fields in this family with conductor $f$, and let ${\mathcal F}'{}_{G,f}^s$ consist of fields with conductor dividing $f$. For $K$ in the family, write $D_K$ for its discriminant, $g_{K/\mathbb Q}$ for its genus number, and $\operatorname{Cl}_K$ for its class group. For $0<\varepsilon<1$, define

$$
C_{\varepsilon}({\mathcal F}_{G,f}^s)=\left[\prod_{K\in{\mathcal F}_{G,f}^s}\frac{|\operatorname{Cl}_K|}{g_{K/\mathbb Q}(\sqrt{|D_K|})^{\varepsilon}}\right]^{1/|{\mathcal F}_{G,f}^s|},
$$

with analogous definitions of $C'_{\varepsilon}({\mathcal F}'{}_{G,f}^s)$ and $C_{\varepsilon}(K)$. Let $r(G)$ be the minimal number of generators of $G$. If $|G|=\prod_{i=1}^t p_i^{n_i}$, put $R(G)=\sum_{i=1}^t n_i$.

**Successive-maxima conjecture.** (i) As $f$ increases from its minimum, the successive maxima of $C_{\varepsilon}({\mathcal F}_{G,f}^s)$, $C'_{\varepsilon}({\mathcal F}'{}_{G,f}^s)$, and $C_{\varepsilon}(K)$ occur, with probability $1$, for conductors satisfying

$$
r(G)\leq\omega(f)\leq R(G).
$$

This property is independent of $\varepsilon$. (ii) For every $0<\varepsilon<1$, each of these sequences of successive maxima is infinite.

The probability-one qualification means that the assertion may fail on a set of conductors of density zero. The statement is motivated by computations of class numbers after removing the genus contribution; the behavior of the number of prime divisors in the indicated interval remains unclear, and the possible even-order wild-ramification exception is explicitly neglected in the source.

356967.title: The zig-zag conjecture for reductions of crystalline representations
356967.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $V_{k,a_p}$ be a two-dimensional crystalline representation of $\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p)$, and let $v_p(a_p)$ be a half-integral slope satisfying

$$
\frac{1}{2}\leq v_p(a_p)\leq\frac{p-1}{2}.
$$

Let $k_0=2v_p(a_p)+2$ modulo $p-1$ be the corresponding exceptional-weight congruence class, set $r=k-2$ and $r_0=k_0-2$, and define

$$
\tau=v_p(c),\qquad t=v_p(k-k_0),
$$

where

$$
c=\frac{a_p^2-\binom{r-v_-}{v_+}\binom{r-v_+}{v_-}p^{r_0}}{pa_p},
$$

with $v_-$ and $v_+$ the largest and smallest integers such that $v_p(a_p)\in(v_-,v_+)$. **Zig-zag conjecture.** For all sufficiently large weights $k\geq k_0$ with $t$ sufficiently large, the semisimplification $\bar V_{k,a_p}$ of the reduction of $V_{k,a_p}$ is

$$
\bar V_{k,a_p}\sim\begin{cases}\operatorname{ind}(\omega_2^{r_0+1+i(p-1)})&\text{if }\tau\in(t+i-1,t+i),\\[2pt]\mu_{\lambda_i}\cdot\omega^{r_0-i}\oplus\mu_{\lambda_i^{-1}}\cdot\omega^{1+i}&\text{if }\tau=t+i,
\end{cases}
$$

for $0\leq i\leq(r_0-1)/2$ when $r_0$ is odd and $0\leq i\leq r_0/2$ when $r_0$ is even, with constants $\lambda_i\in\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p^*$. Thus, as $\tau$ varies through the $t$-line, the reductions alternate between irreducible and reducible representations. This conjecture describes the exceptional cases not covered by the Breuil–Buzzard–Emerton conjecture; the paper proves it in families and establishes several cases, while the full pattern and the precise constants remain the subject of the stated conjectural formulation.

358976.title: The covering-with-Chang-models conjecture
358976.statement:
Assume $
obreak\textsf{NLE}$ and suppose there are unboundedly many Woodin cardinals and strong cardinals. Let $
obreak\textsf{NLE}$ denote the assertion that there is no active $
obreak\textsf{\omega}_1+1$-iterable countable mouse or lbr mouse whose last extender is a long extender. Let $
obreak\textsf{ZFC-Powerset}$ denote ZFC without the powerset axiom. Let $
obreak\textsf{AD}^+$ denote the strengthened axiom of determinacy, and let $
obreak\textsf{Coll}(\omega,<\kappa)$ be the Levy collapse. If $
obreak\kappa$ is a limit of Woodin cardinals and strong cardinals such that either $
obreak\kappa$ is measurable or $
obreak\operatorname{cf}(\kappa)=\omega$, then there is a transitive model $M$ of $
obreak\textsf{ZFC-Powerset}$ satisfying: (1) $
obreak\operatorname{Ord}\cap M=\kappa^+$; (2) $M$ has a largest cardinal $
obreak\nu$; (3) for every generic $
obreak g\subseteq\operatorname{Coll}(\omega,<\kappa)$, defining $
obreak\mathbb{R}^*=\bigcup_{\alpha<\kappa}\mathbb{R}^{V[g\cap\operatorname{Coll}(\omega,\alpha)]}$ and $
obreak\Gamma^*=\{A^g\cap\mathbb{R}^*: \exists\alpha<\kappa\,(A\in\Gamma^\infty_{g\cap\operatorname{Coll}(\omega,\alpha)})\}$, one has

$$
L\left(M,\bigcup_{\alpha<\nu}\alpha^\omega,\Gamma^*,\mathbb{R}^*\right)\vDash\textsf{AD}^+;
$$

and (4), if there is no inner model with a subcompact cardinal, then

$$
L(M)\vDash\textsf{ZFC}+{\wp}(\nu)={\wp}(\nu)^M+\square_\nu.
$$

**Covering with Chang Models conjecture.** The asserted transitive model $M$ exists with all the listed properties. This conjecture is intended to overcome limitations of the core model induction and would yield consequences for the Proper Forcing Axiom, including an inner model with a subcompact cardinal. Its resolution status is not given in the supplied text.

360929.title: General-jump extension of exponential traveling-wave and speed-bound results
360929.statement:
Let $J$ denote the independent jump-size distribution, and let $v_{**}$ be the minimum selected speed. A mean-field limit (MFL) is the deterministic limiting particle-system dynamics, and a traveling-wave solution (TWS) is a traveling-wave MFL. For an MFL initial state $f(0)$, write $f_x(0)$ for its distribution function and define its right-tail exponent through $-\log(1-f_x(0))/x$. Let $v(\zeta)$ denote the speed bound associated with tail exponent $\zeta$, and let $\zeta_{**}$ be the critical exponent. Also write $\mathring f^n(\infty)$ for the stationary distribution of the centered process and $\phi^{**}$ for the TWS with speed $v_{**}$. **General-jump conjecture.** For generally distributed jump sizes, analogs of the exponential-jump traveling-wave existence theorem and the corresponding MFL speed bounds should hold; in particular, if the jump-size distribution satisfies $\alpha>0$, then: (i) the unique TWS exists for every $v\ge v_{**}$ and does not exist for $v<v_{**}$; (ii) if the right-tail exponent is lower bounded by $\zeta\leq\zeta_{**}$, namely

$$
\liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{-\log(1-f_x(0))}{x}\geq\zeta,
$$

then the MFL average speed is at most $v(\zeta)$, and if the liminf is at least $\zeta_{**}$, the average speed equals $v_{**}$; (iii) if the right-tail exponent is upper bounded by $\zeta\leq\zeta_{**}$, namely

$$
\limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{-\log(1-f_x(0))}{x}\leq\zeta,
$$

then the MFL average speed is at least $v(\zeta)$; and (iv)

$$
\mathring f^n(\infty)\Rightarrow\phi^{**}.
$$

Here $\phi^{**}$ is the TWS with speed $v_{**}$. The conjecture extends the paper's exponential-jump traveling-wave and speed estimates to general jump-size distributions, and predicts convergence of centered stationary processes to the critical traveling wave.

368329.title: Keller–Lübeck–Lynd–Semikina conjectures for fusion systems
368329.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a saturated fusion system on a finite $p$-group $S$ of order $p^e$, and let $\alpha$ be a compatible family. Write $s$ for the sectional rank of $S$, and let $r>0$ be the smallest positive integer such that, when $S$ is nonabelian, $S$ has a character of degree $p^r$. The quantities $\operatorname{\mathbf{k}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)$, $\operatorname{\mathbf{w}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)$, and $\operatorname{\mathbf{m}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha,d)$ are defined above; $[S,S]$ denotes the derived subgroup of $S$. **Keller–Lübeck–Lynd–Semikina conjectures.** The following assertions hold: (1) $\operatorname{\mathbf{k}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)=\operatorname{\mathbf{m}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)$; (2) $\operatorname{\mathbf{k}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)\leqslant |S|$; (3) $\operatorname{\mathbf{w}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)\leqslant p^s$; (4) for every positive integer $d$, $\operatorname{\mathbf{m}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha,d)\geqslant 0$; (5) if $S$ is nonabelian, then $\operatorname{\mathbf{m}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha,d')
e 0$ for some $d
e e$; (6) if $S$ is nonabelian, then $r$ is the smallest positive integer such that $\operatorname{\mathbf{m}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha,d-r)
e 0$; and (7a) $\operatorname{\mathbf{k}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)/\operatorname{\mathbf{m}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha,e)$ is at most the number of conjugacy classes of $[S,S]$, while (7b) $\operatorname{\mathbf{k}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)/\operatorname{\mathbf{w}}(\mathcal{F},\alpha)$ is at most the number of conjugacy classes of $S$. These conjectures generalize weight and ordinary weight conjectures from blocks to compatible families on saturated fusion systems. The paper states that they will be verified for nonconstrained fusion systems on an extraspecial group, while the assertions are presented here as the seven conjectures from the cited source.

371188.title: Numerical slope conjecture for ground states of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the unit ball
371188.statement:
Let $B_1$ be the unit ball, let $\beta$ denote the first Dirichlet eigenvalue parameter, and let $Q_b$ be the least-energy (ground state) solution of the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation for $b\in(-\lambda_1,\infty)$. Write $M(Q_b)$ for its mass, let $\mathcal R$ be the corresponding ground state on the whole space, and let $u(t)$ denote the solution with initial condition $u_0$. The standing wave associated with $Q_b$ is $e^{ibt}Q_b$. **Slope conjecture.** For $d\geq1$: (I) if $0<\alpha<4/d$, then for every $b\in(-\lambda_1,\infty)$, 
$$
\partial_bM(Q_b)>0,
$$
 and $e^{ibt}Q_b$ is orbitally stable in $H_0^1(B_1)$; (II) if $\alpha=4/d$, the same positivity and orbital stability hold for every $b\in(-\lambda_1,\infty)$, $M(Q_b)$ increases monotonically with 
$$
\lim_{b\to\infty}M(Q_b)=M(\mathcal R),
$$
 and initial data satisfying $M(u_0)>M(\mathcal R)$ produce solutions that blow up in finite time; (III) if $\alpha>4/d$ (with $\alpha<4/(d-2)$ when $d\geq3$), there is $b^\ast\in(-\lambda_1,\infty)$ such that $M(Q_b)$ increases to a maximum at $b^\ast$ and then decreases to $M(\mathcal R)$, with $\partial_bM(Q_b)>0$ and orbital stability for $b\in(-\lambda_1,b^\ast)$, and $\partial_bM(Q_b)<0$ and instability for $b\in(b^\ast,\infty)$. The unstable branch may lead either to finite-time blow-up or to oscillation between two states. This conjecture is motivated by the Vakhitov–Kolokolov slope condition and the Grillakis–Shatah–Strauss stability method. The source says that these claims are confirmed numerically; the parser supplies no independent resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

372281.title: Coutts et al.'s spectral-calculus optimality conjecture for quantum channel optimization
372281.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$, and $\mathcal{Z}$ be finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces, let $\rho \in \mathsf{D}(\mathcal{X}\otimes \mathcal{Z})$ and $\sigma \in \mathsf{D}(\mathcal{Y}\otimes \mathcal{Z})$ be density operators, and let $\Phi \in \mathsf{C}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y})$ be a completely positive map. Write $J(\Phi)$ for its Choi representation, let $\operatorname{Id}_{L(\mathcal{Z})}$ denote the identity map on $L(\mathcal{Z})$, and let $\Psi_{\rho}\in\mathsf{C}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Z})$ satisfy

$$
(\Phi\otimes \operatorname{Id}_{L(\mathcal{Z})})(\rho)=(\operatorname{Id}_{L(\mathcal{Y})}\otimes\Psi_{\rho})(J(\Phi)).
$$

Define

$$
Y=\operatorname{sign}\left(\sigma-(\Phi\otimes \operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal{Z}})(\rho)\right),
$$

and $H=(\operatorname{Id}_{L(\mathcal{Y})}\otimes\Psi_{\rho}^*)(Y)$. **Coutts et al.'s optimality conjecture.** The map $\Phi$ is an optimal solution to

$$
\min_{\Phi}\ \left\|\sigma-(\Phi\otimes \operatorname{Id}_{\mathcal{Z}})(\rho)\right\|_*
$$

subject to $\Phi\in\mathsf{C}(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y})$, if and only if

$$
\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal{Y}}(HJ(\Phi))\in\operatorname{Herm}(\mathcal{X})
$$

and

$$
H\succeq \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{Y}}\otimes\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal{Y}}(HJ(\Phi)).
$$

The conjecture concerns certification of optimality in the trace-distance, or nuclear-norm, optimization of quantum channels: it claims that the dual certificate can be obtained from the spectral calculus of the Choi matrix of the candidate optimal channel. The paper constructs a counterexample in two-dimensional Hilbert spaces, so the conjecture is disproved.

374765.title: Lv et al.'s generalized Turán conjecture for triangles and expanded paths and cycles
374765.statement:
Let $P_k^{\triangle}$ and $C_k^{\triangle}$ denote the graphs obtained by the relevant expansion of the path $P_k$ and cycle $C_k$, respectively. For graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$, their **join** $G_1\mathbin{\;{\rotatebox{90}{\textnormal{$\small\Bowtie$}}}}G_2$ has vertex set $V(G_1)\cup V(G_2)$ and contains all edges of $G_1$ and $G_2$, together with every edge between $V(G_1)$ and $V(G_2)$. Let $T(n)$ be a balanced complete bipartite graph, let $X,Y$ be its parts with $|X|\le |Y|$, and let $T^+(n)$ be obtained from $T(n)$ by adding an edge inside $X$. For a positive integer $t$, define

$$
S(n,t):=K_t\mathbin{\;{\rotatebox{90}{\textnormal{$\small\BowTie$}}}}T(n-t),\qquad S^+(n,t):=K_t\mathbin{\;{\rotatebox{90}{\textnormal{$\small\BowTie$}}}}T^+(n-t).
$$

For graphs $Q$ and $F$, let $N(Q,F)$ be the number of copies of $Q$ in $F$, and let $\mathrm{ex}(n,Q,F)$ be the maximum number of copies of $Q$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph.

**Lv et al.'s conjecture.** For $k\ge 4$ and sufficiently large $n$,

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,K_3,P_k^{\triangle})=\mathrm{ex}(n,K_3,C_k^{\triangle})=
\begin{cases}
N\left(K_3,S(n,\left\lfloor \frac{k-1}{2}\right\rfloor)\right),&\text{if $k$ is odd},\\
N\left(K_3,S^+(n,\left\lfloor \frac{k-1}{2}\right\rfloor)\right),&\text{if $k$ is even}.
\end{cases}
$$

This extends exact generalized Turán results for several expanded paths and cycles and predicts the extremal triangle counts for all $k\ge 4$ once $n$ is sufficiently large; its resolution is not established in the supplied context.

379197.title: Suppression conjecture for colored Jones polynomials of Whitehead doubles
379197.statement:
Let $K$ be a nontrivial knot, let $N$ be a positive integer, and let $n$ satisfy $\left|n-\frac{N}{2}\right|<N^\delta$ for some $\frac{1}{2}<\delta<\frac{2}{3}$. Write $\hat{J}_{K,2n+1}$ for the polynomial used in the paper, and evaluate it and its derivative at $e^{\frac{2\pi\sqrt{-1}}{N}}$. **Suppression conjecture.** For every nontrivial knot $K$, 

$$
\frac{\hat{J}_{K,2n+1}\left(e^{\frac{2\pi\sqrt{-1}}{N}}\right)}{t\frac{d}{dt}\hat{J}_{K,2n+1}\left(e^{\frac{2\pi\sqrt{-1}}{N}}\right)}=o(N^{-2})
$$

uniformly on $\left|n-\frac{N}{2}\right|<N^\delta$ for some $\frac{1}{2}<\delta<\frac{2}{3}$. The conjecture formalizes the expected suppression of the undifferentiated term in the satellite-knot summation; the paper proves the relevant estimates only for the torus-knot family under consideration, so the assertion for general nontrivial knots remains open.

379350.title: The bounded isometry conjecture for symplectomorphism groups
379350.statement:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed symplectic manifold with symplectic form $\omega$. Let $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$ be its Hamiltonian group and let $\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)$ be the identity component of its symplectomorphism group. For $\phi\in\operatorname{Symp}(M,\omega)$, define

$$
r(\phi):=\sup\{\rho([\phi,f])\mid f\in\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)\},
$$

where $\rho$ is the Hofer norm on $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$ and $[\phi,f]:=\phi f\phi^{-1}f^{-1}$. A symplectomorphism is **bounded** if $r(\phi)<\infty$, and let $\operatorname{BI}_0(M,\omega)$ denote the set of bounded elements of $\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)$.

**Bounded isometry conjecture.** For all $(M,\omega)$,

$$
\operatorname{BI}_0(M,\omega)=\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega).
$$

The conjecture asserts that every bounded symplectomorphism in the identity component is Hamiltonian. It would imply that every non-Hamiltonian element is unbounded, providing an obstruction to extending the Hofer metric to a bi-invariant metric on the full identity component.

379351.title: The extension conjecture for the Hofer metric on symplectomorphism groups
379351.statement:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold, and let $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$ and $\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)$ denote its Hamiltonian group and the identity component of its symplectomorphism group, respectively. The Hofer metric is the bi-invariant metric on $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$.

**Extension conjecture.** For all symplectic manifolds $(M,\omega)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)\ne\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega),
$$

the Hofer metric on $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$ does not extend to a bi-invariant metric on $\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)$.

This is presented as a more accessible conjecture than the bounded isometry conjecture. The preceding theorem shows that an unbounded symplectomorphism obstructs such an extension, while the conjecture claims that no extension exists whenever the identity component is strictly larger than the Hamiltonian group.

380306.title: The factorisation conjecture for the overconvergent $U$ operator
380306.statement:
Let $p\in\{2,3,5\}$, let $r$ range over some open interval containing $\frac{1}{2}$, and let $\mathcal{S}_k(r)$ be the space on which the overconvergent $U$ operator acts. A factorisation of the form

$$
U^{(r)}=A^{(r)}DB^{(r)}
$$

uses matrices $A^{(r)}$ and $B^{(r)}$ with entries in $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_p}$, each congruent to the identity modulo $p$. **The factorisation conjecture.** For all such $p$ and $r$, this factorisation exists, with diagonal entries of $D$ satisfying

$$
\begin{array}{r|c|c|}
 p & D_{ii} & \nu_p D_{ii}\\ \hline
 2 & \dfrac{2^{4i + 1} (3i)!^2 i!^2}{3\cdot (2i)!^4} & 1 + 2 \nu_2\left(\frac{(3i)!}{i!}\right)\\
 3 & \dfrac{3^{3i} (6i)!(2i)!i!}{2\cdot(3i)!^3} & 2i + 2 \nu_3 \left( \frac{(2i)!}{i!}\right)\\
 5 & \dfrac{5^{2i} (10i)!(3i)!^2i!}{3\cdot(5i)!^3(2i)!} & i + 2\nu_5\left(\frac{(3i)!}{i!}\right)\\
\end{array}
$$

The factorisation would make the slopes of $U$ accessible from the diagonal entries of $D$; the claim is open for $p=3$ and $p=5$, although computations of the matrix entries suggest it holds for $r\in(\frac{1}{3},\frac{2}{3})$ in both cases.

380929.title: The polynomial identity for the general rational Gaudin Lax matrix solution
380929.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $c_1,\dots,c_k$ be arbitrary constants. For each $i$, let $\{\vec{J}_i\}$ denote the set of vectors satisfying

$$
\{\vec{J}_i\}=\{\vec{J}\in\mathbb{N}^i:J_1+2J_2+\cdots+iJ_i=i\}.
$$

For $\vec{J}_i$, write $|\vec{J}_i|=\sum_{l=1}^iJ_l$ for its $1$-norm. **The algebraic conjecture.** The following polynomial identity holds:

$$
\sum_{i=0}^k\left(\sum_{\{\vec{J}_i\}}\frac{c_1^{J_1}}{J_1!}\dots\frac{c_i^{J_i}}{J_i!}\lambda^{|\vec{J}_i|}\sum_{\{\vec{J}_{k-i}\}}\frac{c_1^{J_1}}{J_1!}\dots\frac{c_{k-i}^{J_{k-i}}}{J_{k-i}!}\mu^{|\vec{J}_{k-i}|}\right)=\sum_{\{\vec{J}_k\}}\frac{c_1^{J_1}}{J_1!}\dots\frac{c_k^{J_k}}{J_k!}(\lambda+\mu)^{|\vec{J}_k|}.
$$

This identity is proposed as the algebraic step underlying the general analytic solution of the functional equations for the rational Lax matrix. The source supplies no resolution or further evidence for the conjecture, so its status remains open.

380939.title: Morales–Ramis-type conjecture for Newton systems at Darboux points
380939.statement:
Let a Newton system of the form referred to in the source be meromorphically integrable in the Jacobi sense in a neighborhood of a phase curve $\Gamma$ corresponding to a Darboux point. For each $k\in\mathbb{N}$, consider its $k$-th order variational equations and their differential Galois group.

**Differential Galois integrability conjecture.** The identity component of the differential Galois group of the $k$-th order variational equations is Abelian for every $k\in\mathbb{N}$.

This is proposed as an extension of the corresponding theorem for Hamiltonian systems to Newton equations. The paper explains that higher-order differential Galois groups are difficult to analyse and that extending the Hamiltonian result to Newton systems presents theoretical problems, so the assertion remains open.

381131.title: Conjecture on the staircase and stabilization of five-species coefficients
381131.statement:
Let $k,i,j$ be nonnegative integer indices, let $\boldsymbol{i}$ denote the index tuple associated with the identity permutation $\mathrm{id}\in\mathcal{S}_2$, and write

$$
\alpha_{k,i,j}=\alpha_{5,k,\mathrm{id},\boldsymbol{i}}.
$$

**Staircase and stabilization conjecture.** The coefficients satisfy the following properties. First, for $j\geqslant 0$,

$$
\alpha_{k,i,0}=0\quad\text{for }i\geqslant 3k,
$$

$$
\alpha_{k,i,1}=0\quad\text{for }i\geqslant 3(k-1),
$$

$$
\alpha_{k,i,j}=0\quad\text{for }i\geqslant 3(k-\lambda),\qquad \lambda=\left\lfloor\frac{j+1}{3}\right\rfloor.
$$

In particular, $\alpha_{k,1,j}=0$ for $j\geqslant 3k-1$. Second, there exist numbers $\beta_{i,j}$ such that

$$
\alpha_{k,i,j}=\beta_{i,j}\quad\text{for all }k\geqslant i+j+1.
$$

These claims describe a staircase pattern in the coefficients and their eventual stabilization as time increases. They are conjectured from calculations based on the recursions for the five-species Bak–Sneppen model; the source provides no resolution, so their status remains open.

381556.title: Iterated orthogonal extension conjecture from log-canonical centres
381556.statement:
Let $X$ be the space and let $\vphi_L$, $\psi$, $\ell$, $\spH$, $\spE$, $\sigma$, $\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}$, $\lcc$, $\multidl_{}\paren{\vphi_L}$, and $\RTF|\cdot|(t)[\sigma]$ be as in the paper. Assume that $\spH=\spH[\sigma]\oplus\spE$ is the orthogonal decomposition with respect to the squared norm $\RTF|\cdot|(1)[\sigma]$. **Iterated orthogonal extension conjecture.** There exists a constant $b\geq 1$, independent of $\vphi_L$ and $\psi$, such that, after normalising $\log\abs{\ell\psi}\geq b$ on $X$, for every $f\in\spH[\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}+1]/\spH[1]$ one can inductively find $F_\sigma\in\spE$, for $\sigma=1,\dots,\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}$, beginning with $\sigma=\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}$, so that for every such $\sigma$, 
$$
\sum_{j=\sigma}^{\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}}F_j\equiv f\pmod{\multidl_{}\paren{\vphi_L}\cdot\mathcal{I}_{\lcc}}\quad\text{on }X,
$$
 and 
$$
\RTF|F_\sigma|(1)[\sigma]\leq\RTF|F_\sigma|(0)[\sigma]=\RTF|f-\sum_{j=\sigma+1}^{\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}}F_j|(0)[\sigma].
$$
 Consequently, $F=\sum_{\sigma=1}^{\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}}F_\sigma$ is a holomorphic extension of $f$ and, if additionally $\abs\psi\geq1$ on $X$, satisfies 
$$
\RTF|F|(1)[\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}]\leq\sum_{\sigma=1}^{\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}}\RTF|F_\sigma|(1)[\sigma]\leq\sum_{\sigma=1}^{\sigma_{\operatorname{mlc}}}\RTF|F_\sigma|(0)[\sigma].
$$
 The conjecture proposes an iterated extension procedure from log-canonical centres with an $L^2$ estimate; its resolution is not indicated in the supplied text.

381659.title: Bijection between constrained Delannoy paths and Catalan paths avoiding symmetric peaks
381659.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $E\mathcal{P}^{(1)}_{n,n}(NE,EN)$ be the set of Delannoy paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ consisting of north-steps $N=(0,1)$, east-steps $E=(1,0)$, and diagonal-steps $D=(1,1)$ that avoid the patterns $NE$ and $EN$, end with an east step $E$, and are not below $y=x$. Let the second set consist of Catalan paths of size $n+1$ avoiding symmetric peaks, where a symmetric peak is a peak whose maximal mountain has the form $N^iE^i$.

**Delannoy–Catalan bijection conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there exists a bijection between $E\mathcal{P}^{(1)}_{n,n}(NE,EN)$ and the set of Catalan paths of size $n+1$ avoiding symmetric peaks.

This conjecture proposes a direct combinatorial correspondence between a class of constrained Delannoy paths and Catalan paths with a local peak-avoidance condition. The surrounding discussion identifies the related generating-function identity, but the supplied text gives no evidence that this bijection has been proved or disproved.

382052.title: Binomial generating-series conjecture for orthogonal vector spaces
382052.statement:
In the orthogonal vector-space situation, let $\binom{x}{n}$ denote the generalized binomial coefficient, let $\boldsymbol{D}_n$ and $\boldsymbol{B}_n$ denote the corresponding Dynkin types, and let $\frac{\chi}{\mathrm{J}}^{\mathrm{sd}}_d$ and $\mathrm{DT}^{\mathrm{sd}}_d$ be the numerical self-dual invariants. **Binomial generating-series conjecture.** For every integer $n\geqslant 0$,

$$
\frac{\chi}{\mathrm{J}}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{2n}=\binom{1/4}{n},\qquad \mathrm{DT}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{2n}=(-1)^n\binom{1/4}{n},
$$

$$
\frac{\chi}{\mathrm{J}}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{2n+1}=\binom{-1/4}{n},\qquad \mathrm{DT}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{2n+1}=(-1)^n\binom{-1/4}{n}.
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\chi}{\mathrm{J}}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{\boldsymbol{D}_n}q^n=(1+q)^{1/4},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\mathrm{DT}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{\boldsymbol{D}_n}q^n=(1-q)^{1/4},
$$

$$
\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{\chi}{\mathrm{J}}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{\boldsymbol{B}_n}q^n=(1+q)^{-1/4},\qquad \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\mathrm{DT}^{\mathrm{sd}}_{\boldsymbol{B}_n}q^n=(1-q)^{-1/4}.
$$

These formulas extend the observed numerical pattern for orthogonal vector spaces; their status is not resolved in the supplied source.

382460.title: The parking-number identity for arbitrary finite Coxeter systems
382460.statement:
Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible finite Coxeter system with Coxeter number $h$, let $\vec{c}$ be a Coxeter word in $S$, let $p>0$ be an integer coprime to $h$, and let $J\subseteq S$. Define the rational parabolic $\X$-parking numbers by

$$
\Park_{W,p}^{J,\pm}(\X)=\prod_{i=1}^{|J|}\frac{[p\pm e_i^{J,p}]_\X}{[d_i^J]_\X},
$$

where $d_1^J,\ldots,d_{|J|}^J$ are the fundamental degrees of $W_J$, $e_1^{J,p},\ldots,e_{|J|}^{J,p}$ are the exponents or fake degrees of the $W_J$-action on the Galois-conjugate reflection representation dual $\sf{V}_p^*$, and $[k]_\X=1+\X+\cdots+\X^{k-1}$. **The parking-number identity.** The crystallographic identity

$$
\Park_{W,p}^{J,\pm}(\X)=\frac{1}{(\X-1)^r}\sum_{v\in W^{J,\mp}}\sum_{\vec{\omega}\in\cal{D}^{(v)}(\vec{c}^{p})}\X^{|\sf{d}_{\vec{\omega}}|}(\X-1)^{|\sf{e}_{\vec{\omega}}|}
$$

should hold for every irreducible finite Coxeter system, with the same notation and the sign flip as in the crystallographic theorem. This would extend the stated parking-number formula beyond crystallographic Coxeter systems to the full irreducible finite Coxeter setting.

382565.title: The classification of numerically elementary $(-1)$-curves with $b4<2bc_1$
382565.statement:
Let $(\delta;\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_r)$ be the numerical data of an elementary $(-1)$-curve in the relevant blow-up of projective space, where $\delta$ is its degree and $\mu_1$ is the largest multiplicity among the assigned points. Such a curve is **numerically elementary** when its numerical data satisfy the equalities defining an elementary $(-1)$-curve.

**Classification conjecture.** The only numerically elementary $(-1)$-curves satisfying $\delta<2\mu_1$ are the lines through two points.

The examples preceding the conjecture exhibit numerical sequences satisfying the defining equalities but not corresponding to elementary $(-1)$-curves; together with the stated proposition, they motivate this proposed classification.

394120.title: Lens spaces bounding rational homology balls and the ribbon conjecture for 2-bridge knots
394120.statement: Let $p>q>0$ be coprime integers. Define $R\subset\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ as the smallest subset such that $f(R)\subseteq R$ and $g(R)\subseteq R$, where, for $p/q\in\mathbb{Q}_{>0}$ with $p>q>0$ and $(p,q)=1$, $f(p/q)=p/(p-q)$ and $g(p/q)=p/q'$ with $p>q'>0$ and $qq'\equiv1\pmod p$, and such that $R$ contains every $p/q$ with $p=m^2$ for some $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and $q$ of one of the following types: (1) $mk\pm1$ with $m>k>0$ and $(m,k)=1$; (2) $d(m\pm1)$, where $d>1$ divides $2m\mp1$; or (3) $d(m\pm1)$, where $d>1$ is odd and divides $m\pm1$. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $p/q\in R$; (2) there exist a surface $\Sigma$ with boundary, homeomorphic to a disk if $p$ is odd and to the disjoint union of a disk and a Möbius band if $p$ is even, together with a ribbon immersion $i:\Sigma\looparrowright S^3$ satisfying $i(\partial\Sigma)=K(p,q)$; and (3) the lens space $L(p,q)$ smoothly bounds a rational homology $4$-ball. Consequently, for odd $p$, the 2-bridge knot $K(p,q)$ is ribbon if and only if it is smoothly slice; hence the ribbon conjecture holds for 2-bridge knots.

399483.title: Discrete Riemann mapping conjecture
399483.statement: Suppose $\Omega$ is a Jordan domain in the complex plane. Take three distinct points $p,q,r$ in the boundary of $\Omega$. For each $\epsilon>0$, let $\Omega_\epsilon$ be a maximum simply connected domain in $\Omega$ which has a triangulation $A_\epsilon$ by equilateral triangles of edge length $\epsilon$. Take three vertices $p_\epsilon,q_\epsilon,r_\epsilon$ in the boundary of $\Omega_\epsilon$ so that $d(p,p_\epsilon)<2\epsilon$, $d(q,q_\epsilon)<2\epsilon$, and $d(r,r_\epsilon)<2\epsilon$. Let the metric double of $(\Omega_\epsilon,A_\epsilon)$ along the boundary be the polyhedral 2-sphere $(S^2,B_\epsilon,d_\epsilon)$. Using Theorem 1, produce a new polyhedral metric $(S^2,T_\epsilon,d^*_\epsilon)$ such that its area is $\sqrt{3}/2$, $d^*_\epsilon$ is discrete conformal to $d_\epsilon$, the discrete curvatures of $d^*_\epsilon$ at $p_\epsilon,q_\epsilon,r_\epsilon$ are $4\pi/3$, and the discrete curvatures at all other vertices are zero. The conjecture is that, as $\epsilon\to0$, $(S^2,T_\epsilon,d^*_\epsilon)$ converges to the metric double of the unit equilateral triangle.

399559.title: Conjecture A on graded Cartan invariants of symmetric groups and Hecke algebras
399559.statement:
Let $H_n(\xi)$ be the Iwahori–Hecke algebra of type $A_{n-1}$ over a field containing a primitive $\ell$-th root of unity $\xi$, let $A=\mathbb{Z}[v,v^{-1}]$, and let $C^{v}_{H_n(\xi)}$ be its graded Cartan matrix. Conjecture A states that
\[
C^{v}_{H_n(\xi)}\equiv_A \operatorname{diag}\left(\left\{r_v^{\ell}(\lambda)\mathrel{}\middle|\mathrel{}\lambda\vdash n\text{ and }\ell\nmid\lambda_i\ \forall i\right\}\right),
\]
where, for a partition $\lambda$ of $n$,
\[
r_v^{\ell}(\lambda)=\prod_{k\ge 1}\prod_{t=1}^{\left\lfloor m_k(\lambda)/\ell\right\rfloor}\left[\ell k\,t_{\pi(\ell^k)}\right]_{(\ell,k)\,t_{\pi(\ell^k)'}}.
\]
Here $m_k(\lambda)$ is the multiplicity of the part $k$, $\pi(\ell^k)$ is the set of prime divisors of $\ell^k$, $t_{\pi(\ell^k)}$ denotes the largest divisor of $t$ whose prime divisors lie in $\pi(\ell^k)$, and $[s]_u=(v^{su}-v^{-su})/(v^u-v^{-u})$. The notation in the report labels the factor in the displayed definition as $r_\ell(\lambda)$, although the diagonal entries are written $r_v^{\ell}(\lambda)$; this is a notational inconsistency in the source.

400138.title: Conjecture on absolute linear Harbourne constants
400138.statement:
Let a configuration of lines \(\mathcal L=\{L_1,\ldots,L_d\}\) in \(\mathbb P^2(K)\) have singular points \(\mathcal P(\mathcal L)=\{P_1,\ldots,P_s\}\), and let \(m_{\mathcal L}(P_k)\) be the number of lines through \(P_k\). Define
\[
H(K,\mathcal L)=\frac{d^2-\sum_{k=1}^s m_{\mathcal L}(P_k)^2}{s},\qquad H(K,d)=\min_{\mathcal L}H(K,\mathcal L),\qquad H(d)=\min_K H(K,d),
\]
where the last minimum is over all fields \(K\). For \(d\ge 2\), let \(q=q(d)\) be the least number of the form \(q=p^r\), with \(p\) prime and \(r\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), such that \(d\le q^2+q+1\), and put \(i=q^2+q+1-d\). If \(i\le 2q-2\), then
\[
H(d)=h(d),
\]
where
\[
h(d)=\frac{q^2+q+1-i-\varepsilon_1(i)m_1(i)-\varepsilon_2(i)m_2(i)-t_{q-1}(i)(q-1)-t_q(i)q-t_{q+1}(i)(q+1)}{\varepsilon_1(i)+\varepsilon_2(i)+t_{q-1}(i)+t_q(i)+t_{q+1}(i)},
\]
with
\[
m_1(i)=q+1-i,\qquad m_2(i)=2q+1-i,
\]
\[
\varepsilon_1(i)=\begin{cases}1&0\le i\le q-1,\\0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\qquad
\varepsilon_2(i)=\begin{cases}1&i>q+1,\\0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\]
\[
t_{q-1}(i)=\begin{cases}qi-q^2-q&i>q+1,\\0&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}
\]
\[
t_q(i)=\begin{cases}qi&i\le q+1,\\2q^2-(i-2)q-1&i>q+1,\end{cases}\qquad
t_{q+1}(i)=\begin{cases}q^2+q-iq&i\le q+1,\\0&i>q+1.\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, when \(i=2q-1\),
\[
H(d)=-\frac{q^3+q^2-2q+2}{q^2+q-1}.
\]
